rationale: bugs_open/270: the discovery check `missing_structure` reads pages.rendered_header/rendered_footer/rendered_head to decide whether a site's chrome needs rebuilding, but those three columns are empty on all 694 pages fleet-wide (chrome moved to site_components, written by render_site_components, some time ago; the pages columns are vestigial — standing LANDMINES.md entry, 2026-08-03). A second filter in the same query, pages.status IN ('active','deployed'), is also non-discriminating: pages.status takes exactly two live values, active/archived; 'deployed' is a value of a DIFFERENT column (build_status) and never occurs here. Together the predicate is true for every non-archived page on every site, unconditionally. Verified live 2026-08-15: 50 needs_rerender work items filed under item_key missing_structure:rerender since 2026-04-24, ~31 completed (each a full-site reassembly dispatched at severity=high/priority=30, ahead of real queued work), still firing as of 2026-08-14 -- i.e. every single discovery pass on every site with an active page, for four months straight. The misleading reason string this check writes ('Pages deployed without header/footer -- likely built before site_components were rendered') has already misled two other bug investigations (bugs_open/232, bugs_open/235) into reasoning about a defect that was never real. This submission retypes the predicate to the table chrome actually lives in and adds the framework's own self-resolution mechanism (RFC_010's CheckResult.Resolved) so the ~17 currently-open false items close themselves on each affected site's next discovery pass, with no hand-written cleanup SQL. Full evidence and the weighing of this fix against the alternative (retiring the check outright in favour of a newer, approved-but-not-yet-enabled check) is in docs/agent_docs/docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_270_missing_structure/PLAN_2026-08-15_missing_structure_check.md.

plan.summary: Retype check_missing_structure.go's predicate from the vestigial pages.rendered_header/footer/head columns to the real chrome store, site_components, keying health on non-empty rendered_html per slot (header/footer/head), not on build_status (which coexists with valid serving content while a re-render is merely scheduled). Keep the check's name, item_type and item_key unchanged so no config change is needed and the framework's existing retraction mechanism (CheckResult.Resolved) can close the historical false-positive items itself. Add a unit test file that asserts on the actual SQL text issued, so a future regression back to the broken columns cannot hide behind a green happy-path test.

edits.rationale: The existing predicate cannot be false -- it queries columns that are empty fleet-wide. This is the entire defect; every other change in the file follows from fixing this one query.
edits.sketch: Replace the per-page pages.rendered_header/footer/head query with one row of four EXISTS booleans against site_components (header_ok/footer_ok/head_ok keyed on coalesce(length(rendered_html),0)>0, plus has_active_pages from pages.status='active'). Delete findPagesWithMissingStructure and missingStructureFinding (per-page plumbing on top of a site-level fact). Three branches replace the old single path: (1) all three slots healthy -> empty Findings/WorkItems plus one CheckResult.Resolved{ItemType:"needs_rerender", ItemKey:"missing_structure:rerender", Reason:...} -- narrow ItemKey, not AllOfType, since this check only ever owns that one key per site; (2) any slot unhealthy AND has_active_pages -> one Finding plus one WorkItemSpec identical in shape to today's (same ItemType/Severity/Priority/HandlerAgent/ItemKey) except Summary and the SpecJSON reason text, which now name the real predicate instead of the old guessed-history string; (3) any slot unhealthy AND zero active pages -> log at Info, return empty result, no finding/item/retraction (nothing to reassemble, and no claim we have grounds to make). A query error returns immediately as an error, which is what makes the runner skip the Resolved step entirely (discovery_checks.go:266-269) -- RFC_010's safety property that a blinded check cannot retract real defects.

edits.rationale: sqlmock-fed happy-path tests alone would stay green even if the query silently reverted to the broken pages.rendered_* columns or started gating on build_status -- sqlmock returns whatever rows a test hands it regardless of the WHERE clause actually issued. The check_componentless_pages_test.go file in the same package already establishes the pattern for guarding against exactly this.
edits.sketch: Five tests: (1) all-healthy fixture -> zero findings/items, one narrow Resolved retraction with a non-empty reason; (2) one unhealthy slot + active pages -> one work item under the UNCHANGED item_key missing_structure:rerender, Summary names the slot, SpecJSON does not carry the old 'likely built before' guessed-history text; (3) unhealthy + zero active pages -> nothing at all; (4) query error propagates as an error (not swallowed); (5) asserts the missingStructureQuery constant's text: references site_components and length(rendered_html), never pages.rendered_(header|footer|head), never build_status, never the literal 'deployed'.

LANDMINES.md, "pages.rendered_header / rendered_footer / rendered_head are VESTIGIAL" (2026-08-03): chrome lives in site_components, written by render_site_components; the pages columns are read by (at the time of that entry) exactly one caller, check_missing_structure.go
LANDMINES.md, "include_statuses ... 'deployed' NEVER OCCURS" (2026-08-03): pages.status vs pages.build_status are different columns with overlapping vocabularies

registry.go:84-112, CheckResult.Resolved doc comment (RFC_010, owner ruling 2026-08-02): a retraction fires only on a positive observation, never inferred from an empty Findings slice; the runner skips Resolved entirely when Run returns an error
discovery_checks.go:266-283: Resolved entries are applied in the same transaction as WorkItem inserts, after them, only reachable when the check did not error

chrome_link_policy.go:127-137: build_status='pending' on site_components is the supported 're-render scheduled' signal, set while rendered_html still holds valid, currently-serving content -- the reason this fix keys health on rendered_html content, not build_status
bugs_open/232, bugs_open/235: both bug investigations had to reason around a missing_structure work item's misleading reason text before concluding it was not a real defect
plan.risks: The retyped predicate ('a site's chrome is healthy iff site_components holds non-empty rendered_html for all three slots') is a materially different signal from the old one and a reviewer should check whether it could produce a NEW false positive the old one didn't. The one documented edge case: on 2026-08-03 a site (loanandmortgagecalculator.co.uk) served full chrome on 41 pages while holding ZERO site_components rows, because an older pipeline had baked chrome directly into deployed page artefacts rather than writing site_components. That state does not exist anywhere in the live fleet today (that specific site was backfilled since; every currently-serving site has 3/3 rendered site_components rows, verified 2026-08-15) but the class could in principle return if a legacy-style write path is ever reintroduced -- in which case this check would file one (correct-looking but for the wrong reason) work item, order a reassembly, and the reassembly would converge the site onto site_components the same way nav-updater did for the 2026-08-03 case, after which the check goes quiet again. This is a bounded, self-terminating false positive versus the unbounded always-fire behaviour being replaced, but a reviewer with more context on whether baked-chrome write paths still exist anywhere should weigh in. Second, smaller risk: the fix changes the WorkItemSpec's Summary and SpecJSON reason text; nothing was found (grep across *.go/*.sql/*.yaml/*.py/*.sh/*.ts/*.js) that parses either field programmatically, but a reviewer closer to the rerender-pages handler should confirm it doesn't pattern-match on the old reason string anywhere outside this repo's own grep reach.
